fatal_errors: Identifies CoCrFeNiTi rather than the FCC/BCC Al-Cr-Fe-Ni multilayer with a 16 nm modulation period.
Replaces interface-coherency control by mechanical alloying and spark-plasma sintering, omitting the coherent, semicoherent, and grain-boundary interface comparison.
Uses hypothetical high-temperature bulk-creep conditions instead of room-temperature nanoindentation creep at 5 mN.
Does not reconstruct the central semicoherent-interface mechanism involving dislocation blocking, pileup, and proposed interfacial amorphization-assisted diffusion or interface slip.
Invents a 20% creep-resistance improvement, temperature and stress ranges, and a 15% falsification threshold without supporting evidence.
The cited evidence reports general HEA properties and MA/SPS-induced hardness and strength, not creep measurements or a diffusion-to-dislocation creep transition.
explanation: The hypothesis only aligns at the broad level of discussing an HEA and diffusion- versus dislocation-mediated creep. It misses the target material, multilayer architecture, modulation-period intervention, interface-coherency mediator, nanoindentation conditions, comparison baselines, and measured stress-exponent results. Its proposed experiment could compare creep resistance but does not measure stress exponents or otherwise discriminate the two creep mechanisms. Neither cited source supports the claimed creep transition or quantitative improvement, so this is not a well-supported alternative.
